lesson_yaml:
schema: cairn/lesson/v0.1
id: java-wicket-upload-path-traversal-unvalidated-filename
title: Upload file path built from client-supplied name or field id without canonical containment check
summary: A file path is built directly from a client-supplied upload file name or field id, for example
  `new File(new File(base, fieldId), clientFileName)`. Values such as `../../x` escape the base folder,
  allowing arbitrary file write or read. The path must be canonicalized and checked to start with the
  base directory before use.
cwe:
- CWE-22
severity: high
confidence: medium
languages:
- java
source:
  kind: fix-commit
  ref: 72470983f689c61e6a6c0b7388ef955f23bb1e16
  vulnerable_ref: 72470983f689c61e6a6c0b7388ef955f23bb1e16^
  patched_ref: 72470983f689c61e6a6c0b7388ef955f23bb1e16
  repository: https://github.com/apache/wicket
rule:
  message: 'A file path is built from a client-controlled upload file name or field id without a canonical-path

    containment check. This permits path traversal (`../`). Resolve the canonical path

    (getCanonicalFile/toRealPath) and verify it stays within the base folder.

    '
  patterns:
  - pattern-either:
    - pattern: new File($BASE, $UP.getClientFileName())
    - pattern: new java.io.File($BASE, $UP.getClientFileName())
    - patterns:
      - pattern-inside: "$R $M(..., String $ID, String $NAME, ...) {\n  ...\n}\n"
      - pattern-either:
        - pattern: new File(new File($B, $ID), $NAME)
        - pattern: new java.io.File(new java.io.File($B, $ID), $NAME)
    - patterns:
      - pattern-inside: "$R $M(..., FileUpload $F, String $ID, ...) {\n  ...\n}\n"
      - pattern-either:
        - pattern: new File($B, $ID)
        - pattern: new java.io.File($B, $ID)
  - pattern-not-inside: new File(...).getCanonicalFile()
  - pattern-not-inside: new java.io.File(...).getCanonicalFile()
  - pattern-not-inside: new File(...).getCanonicalPath()
fix:
  guidance: Never combine a client-supplied file name or upload field id with the base folder directly.
    Resolve the base folder with toRealPath, resolve the target with getCanonicalFile, and reject with
    a SecurityException unless the canonical target path startsWith the canonical base (and upload sub-folder).
    Use one shared resolver for both save and getFile.
  example: "Path base = getFolder().toPath().toRealPath();\njava.io.File dir = new File(getFolder(), uploadFieldId).getCanonicalFile();\n\
    if (!dir.toPath().startsWith(base)) {\n    throw new SecurityException(\"Path traversal detected in\
    \ uploadFieldId\");\n}\njava.io.File target = new File(dir, clientFileName).getCanonicalFile();\n\
    if (!target.toPath().startsWith(dir.toPath())) {\n    throw new SecurityException(\"Path traversal\
    \ detected in client filename\");\n}\n"
